description: The Norse gods are worshipped in Scandinavia; the earliest evidence is archaeological (runestones, offerings, place-names). The gods Odin, Thor, and others are named.
The Viking Age. Skaldic poetry names the gods. The great ship burials (Oseberg, c. 834; Gokstad) and the Gosforth Cross (c. 950–1000) show the gods in art.
Scandinavia converts to Christianity; the old gods are suppressed but survive in poetry and place-names.
Snorri Sturluson writes the Prose Edda, preserving the myths in a Christian context. This is the main source for most Norse myth.
The Poetic Edda (Codex Regius) is copied, preserving older oral poetry (the Hávamál, the Völuspá, and others).
